main_text.l: lis suis, & qui corā seipsis sunt prudentes. Væ qui fortes sunt ad bibedum vinū,quiq; viri sunt robusti ad miscedam ebrietatem. Qui iustificant impiū propter munus: iustitiam aūt iustorū auferūt ab eis. Propterea sicut devorat stipulam lingua ignis,& glu-mā flamma dissoluit, (sic) radix eorū quasi putredo erit, & germen eorū quasi pulvis ascedet:quoniam abiecerūt legem Domi-ni exercituū, & eloquiū sancti (Dei) Israel detestati sunt. Idcirco exarsit furor Domini in populum suum, & extedens manum sua super eum percussit eum:& cotremue-rūt mōtes, fuitq; cadauer eorū lacerū proiectū in medio platearū: & in omnib. istis non est aversus furor eius,sed adhuc manus eius est extēta.Et levabit signū ad gentes è longinquo,& sibilū dabit ei ab extremitate terrę,& ecce velociter & levis aduenie[?]. Non erit ullus lassus neq; impingés in eo, nullus dormitabit aut dormiet:non solue-tur cingulū lumborū eius, neq; rumpetur corrigia calciamentorū eius.Sed & sagittæ illius sunt acutę,& omnes arcus eius exten-ti: ungulæ equorū eius quasi silex reputa-tæ sunt,& rotæ eius quasi turbo.Rugitus il-lius sicut leonis, fremet sicut catuli leonis,

page.notes: The text is continuous across the page; no indented paragraph starts on this page, so it is one paragraph. The first word "lis" is the end of a word from the previous page ("iis"), printed without a leading I visible. The catchword "&c" at lower right is uncertain; the mark is stylised. The form "è" (for "de") and "aduenie" (probably "adueniet") are doubtful readings. "extedens", "fuitq;" and "impingés" are kept as printed. The line "ad gentes è" is doubtful at the "è". The hyphens in "glu-mā", "Domi-ni", "cotremue-rūt", "pro-iectū", "solue-tur", "exten-ti", "reputa-tæ" and "il-lius" are printed line-end hyphens and are kept. The marginal "&" at the right of the last line is a printed catchword, not a margin note; it is shown as a note only because its position is at the margin. The word "iustitiam" is split at the line end without a visible hyphen and is written whole.
